Subject: MAP input: acceptance signals and smoke tests

Rishi —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and the engineering team asked me to capture a single source of truth for the MAP so legal/procurement can align with engineering on an operational acceptance bar. Specifically we need:

- Concrete pass/fail items for the pilot (what is 'good enough' to move to a paid pilot)
- Cutover smoke tests for the first two weeks of production
- A suggested timeline (mutual action plan) that ties those tests to procurement milestones

I attached CoreHealth_requirements.pdf with our initial expectations. Can you send a short formal acceptance ladder and a smoke-test checklist we can include in the MAP? Our procurement lead will need it by Fri 8 Apr for review.

Appreciate it,
Anita Shah
VP, Digital Platforms
CoreHealth

Attachments: CoreHealth_requirements.pdf (pdf, 1 page summary)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP input: acceptance signals and smoke tests

Anita —

Thanks — attached is a concise acceptance ladder (MAP_acceptance_ladder_v3.xlsx) and a short operational smoke test runbook (smoke_tests_runbook.md). High level summary below so procurement/engineering can quickly paste into the MAP: please confirm and we'll finalize for DocuSign.

Acceptance ladder (4 tiers) — what to measure and who signs off:
1) Discovery pass (pre-pilot) — engineering demo, API connectivity, basic hallucination check
   - Evidence: demo recording + sample inference logs
   - Sign-off: CoreHealth Engineering Lead + Redwood Solutions (Karthik)
2) Pilot functional (feature-level) — feature acceptance on 3 canonical prompts, 95% intent-match vs baseline, hallucination rate <=1.5% on eval set
   - Evidence: evaluation report (scripted tests) + sample traffic capture
   - Sign-off: CoreHealth Product Manager + Redwood AE (Marissa)
3) Operational run (load/latency) — sustained P95 latency <=300ms (95th percentile) at expected concurrent requests; token-cost within agreed range +/-10%
   - Evidence: perf dashboard snapshot (2x 1-hour windows), cost report
   - Sign-off: CoreHealth SRE + Redwood Infra (Rishi)
4) Cutover readiness (security & compliance) — SOC2 evidence checklist items validated, audit logs available, KMS integrated for keys
   - Evidence: SOC2 artifact, test audit log pull, KMS verification
   - Sign-off: CoreHealth Security + Redwood Security

Operational smoke tests (first 14 days) — runbook highlights:
- Day 0 (post-cutover): 5 end-to-end sanity flows, compare to pilot baseline; check token accounting and retry logic
- Day 1–3: traffic ramp to 25/50/100% of projected throughput with P95 checks at each step
- Daily (D1–D14): sample 200 requests across key routes; run automated hallucination detector (scripted) and threshold alerts if >1.5%
- Week 1 checkpoint: post-cutover retrospective and rollback criteria review (see rollback triggers in sheet)

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Functional: pass = 3/3 canonical prompts match expected intent classification; any failure requires remediation and re-run
- Latency: pass = P95 <= 300ms for the agreed traffic mix over 1-hour window
- Cost: pass = observed per-token cost <= agreed estimate * 1.1 over pilot window
- Security: pass = audit log entries retrievable for last 24 hours and KMS key rotation success message

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm the thresholds above (especially latency and hallucination tolerance)
- We finalize the MAP doc and attach the two artifacts; Marissa will generate the mutual action timeline and link procurement steps to sign-off rows

I'll be available Mon/Tue to walk through with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_acceptance_ladder_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), smoke_tests_runbook.md (text runbook)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Anita — quick notes from AE side after reviewing Rishi's ladder:

- Pilot functional: recommend changing intent-match threshold to '>=94%' with a required re-run if between 90–94% (gives room for small sample variance)
- Operational run latency: aim for P95 <= 250ms as stretch; use 300ms as contractual pass but document 250ms as target for post-cutover optimization plan
- Add procurement row linking DocuSign milestone to the "Pilot functional" sign-off (so commercial can trigger billing once functional pass is confirmed)

I'll draft the MAP timeline and attach to this thread by EOD Tue so procurement has a one-click DocuSign bundle. Rishi — can you add the exact perf dashboard screenshots we expect people to capture for evidence? (Just filenames are fine.)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
